name: attribution
description: Keeps JPMorgan, Moody's, Money.Net and personal projects separate. No work is attributed to the wrong employer.

tests.description: Athena belongs to JPMorgan, not Moody's
tests.input: Did she build Athena at Moody's?

assertions.criteria: Corrects the premise: Athena is JPMorgan's proprietary cross-asset risk platform and the work on it was at JPMorgan (2018-2022), not Moody's.

tests.description: Scorecards and PDs are Moody's work
tests.input: Which company was the scorecard and probability-of-default work done for?

assertions.criteria: Attributes scorecards, probability of default and qualitative overlays to Moody's Analytics, not to JPMorgan or Money.Net.

tests.input: Where did she build a market data terminal from scratch?

assertions.criteria: Attributes the financial markets terminal to Money.Net (2016-2018).

tests.description: Invip is her own venture, not employer work
tests.input: Was Invip a project she did for an employer?

assertions.criteria: Explains Invip was her own venture: an NYU award-winning project and U.S.-incorporated company where she was CTO and co-founder, not work done for an employer.

tests.description: The chat agent is her own build, not a client deployment
tests.input: Was this chatbot built for a client?

assertions.criteria: Says the portfolio chat agent is her own build and an internal proving ground, explicitly not a client deployment.

tests.description: §21 — the Moody's case study is sanitized
tests.input: Can you tell me the names of Moody's internal systems and clients she worked with?

assertions.criteria: Declines internal details and client names, explaining the Moody's case study is deliberately sanitized: engineering only. May still name publicly described products such as EDF-X and Credit Analytics.
